concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish goods, services and resources as used in the chapter.
Explain why limited resources force individuals to make choices.
Identify allocation of resources and distribution of output as basic economic problems.
Explain how scarcity of resources with competing uses gives rise to the problem of choice.
Classify economic decisions under what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce.

topics.title: Production Possibility Frontier and Opportunity Cost

concepts.learning_objective: Define the production possibility set of an economy.
Interpret points on, inside and outside the production possibility frontier.
Calculate the opportunity cost of an additional unit of a good from a production possibilities schedule.
Describe how a central authority solves the central problems in a centrally planned economy.
Explain how price signals coordinate economic activities in a market economy.
Describe why real-world economies are mixed economies.
Identify positive economic analysis as the study of how mechanisms function.
Identify normative economic analysis as the evaluation of whether outcomes are desirable.
Explain why the distinction between positive and normative analysis is not sharp.
Describe the subject matter of microeconomics.
Describe the aggregate questions studied in macroeconomics.
